To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temperature distribution in machining of Al-SiCp composite is affected by cutting speed and depth of cut.
the temperature distribution at the tool edge is affected by cutting speed and depth of cut.
FEA can be used to model the temperature rise in machining of MMC and the results can be used for the prediction of temperature rise in cutting of MMC.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an experimental procedure for determining the temperature in the cutting zone in machining of A1/SICP composites and to study the temperature distribution in machining of A/SiCp composites.
the development of new materials for use in the aerospace industry.
the study of the effect of the temperature on the cutting tool edge, frictional heat generated at the tool flank face and the work tool interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temperature distribution in orthogonal machining of Al/SiCp MMC is influenced by cutting parameters and cutting tool material.
, this paper presents a study on the temperature prediction in orthogonal machining of A1/Sicp composites using FEA.
the temperature at the tool-chip interface increases with the cutting speed and depth of cut.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temperature distribution at the interface region is more than the temperature distribution at other regions.
the temperature distribution at the cutting edge, shear plane, and tool-work interface has been obtained by using FEA.
the temperature distribution at the interface of workpiece and cutting tool has been studied and the maximum temperature at the cutting tool edge has been calculated using thermocouples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature of the cutting tool and the cutting zone can be predicted by using the finite element analysis and the temperature can be controlled to some extent.
the temperature of the workpiece and cutting tool can be reduced by optimizing the process parameters.
the use of a composite tool insert in turning of Al/SiCp composite leads to lower tool wear and higher tool life than a carbide tool insert.
